ia-board-chair.summary: The County Supervisor District card names your supervisors but never says which of them chairs the board — the officer who sets the agenda and signs for the county.
ia-board-chair.why: Every statewide source that names Iowa's supervisors lists them as a flat group; the chair is chosen by the board itself each January and no publisher records that choice in one place.
ia-board-chair.wanted: One publisher that records which supervisor chairs each board and keeps it current through the January reorganisation — most naturally the association whose directory already names every supervisor.

ia-municipal-officeholders.summary: The City card names your city and nothing else — not your mayor, not your council, not your clerk. That is true in 931 of Iowa's 939 cities; eight publish a page readable enough to name the people who run them.
ia-municipal-officeholders.why: No one publishes Iowa's city officeholders in one place, and the cities do not publish alike: two in five have no website at all, and a survey of every city website that exists found a roster a machine could read on sixteen of them.
ia-municipal-officeholders.wanted: A statewide list of Iowa's city clerks or councils from one publisher — the shape Wisconsin's Elections Commission supplies for its 1,848 municipalities. Failing that, a city's own council page, or a county publishing its officials as data.

johnson-county-supervisor-districts.summary: Johnson County's supervisor card names the county and says its districts are pending — it cannot yet tell you which of the five you live in.
johnson-county-supervisor-districts.why: The county adopted five districts for the November 2026 election but publishes them only as a printed map, and the statewide layer this app reads still carries the county under its older at-large form.
johnson-county-supervisor-districts.wanted: A map of the five districts the county can share as data, or a link to one — the way Black Hawk County publishes its own.

jones-county-supervisor.summary: Jones County carries no supervisor-district card at all — the county is entirely absent from the state's own statewide aggregate.
jones-county-supervisor.why: The Iowa Legislature's own CountySupervisorDistricts layer is this app's only statewide source, and Jones County has zero rows in it — measured both by name and by its own FIPS code (105), not a naming mismatch.
jones-county-supervisor.wanted: The county's own GIS file for the districts its own map already shows, or the state adding Jones to its statewide aggregate. Not an extraction from that published map — it carries no usable shapes, which was measured rather than assumed.
